items.statement: Weekly report completion in the week after an unanswered severe alert is lower than in the week after an answered one, and the difference is larger for patients aged 75 or over.
items.rationale: Directly tests the mechanism suggested by claims c3 and c6 with data the platform already records; the answer changes the response standard.
items.risks: Alerts left unanswered may cluster in sicker patients who stop for other reasons.

items.statement: Offering weekly reporting to new patients in the two remaining clinics reduces emergency visits over three cycles compared with usual telephone triage.
items.rationale: The effectiveness question is already answered by trials (claims c1 and c5), and the rollout decision removes equipoise.
items.risks: No funding, no equipoise, and too few patients in two clinics.

items.statement: Patients living in the most deprived areas stop reporting earlier than others, and a paper route closes most of the gap.
items.rationale: Completion is lower in deprived areas (claim c2) and paper is often preferred by older patients.
items.risks: A paper route cannot be added to the platform before June 2027.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the delivery mechanism to test, h2 kept visible as the trial question.
